Self-hosted auth: $0 per user, but what you pay instead

Answer: Better Auth (MIT) and Auth.js (ISC) charge $0 per user, but you pay for email, SMS, database/hosting and engineer time. With our stated assumptions (1 transactional email per user per month on Amazon SES at $0.10 per 1,000, no SMS, existing database), the cash cost is $1/mo at 10k users and $10/mo at 100k. The cheapest hosted plan in our ledger lists $0/mo at 10k (Clerk Hobby) and $0/mo at 100k (WorkOS AuthKit), so on cash alone self-hosting does not beat free tiers. Against paid plans it can: at 100k users Clerk Pro lists $1,025/mo and Firebase / Identity Platform $275/mo, so at an assumed $100/hour self-hosting saves money only while upkeep stays under 10.2 h/mo (vs Clerk Pro) or 2.6 h/mo (vs Firebase).

Do teams still build authentication from scratch, or is there a fair indie alternative?

Few write it from scratch. Open-source libraries run inside your app and database with no per-user fee: Better Auth (MIT license) and Auth.js (ISC license; the Auth.js project is now part of Better Auth). The fair trade: no MAU bill, but you own the email, SMS, database and upkeep costs below. Sources: Better Auth on GitHub (MIT), authjs.dev.

Clerk vs Better Auth: when does self-hosting actually save money?

Up to 25k–50k users, Clerk Hobby (50k MRU), Auth0 Free (25k MAU) and Firebase (50k MAU) all list $0, and WorkOS AuthKit lists free to 1M MAU (SSO billed per connection), so self-hosting can’t save cash there. Its case is control, data location, and free-tier feature limits (e.g. Clerk Hobby lists no MFA). Once you need a paid plan, the gap opens: Clerk Pro goes from $25/mo at 50k to $1,025/mo at 100k, and Auth0 B2C Essentials lists $3,500/mo at 50k. That is where self-hosting can earn its upkeep, if your team’s hours stay under the break-even in the table. Compare: Clerk pricing · Auth0 pricing · Firebase / Identity Platform pricing · Descope pricing.

Every auth provider raises prices if you require SSO. Does self-hosting avoid the SSO tax?

Better Auth’s SSO plugin supports OIDC, OAuth2 and SAML 2.0, so there is no per-connection license fee when you self-host; you still carry setup and support for each customer’s IdP. Its optional managed infrastructure lists self-service SSO at 1 connection, then $50/month per connection (on the $20/mo Infrastructure Pro plan). Hosted per-connection list prices in our ledger: Clerk Pro $75, Auth0 Essentials (B2B) $100, WorkOS AuthKit $125, Descope Pro $50. Sources: Better Auth SSO plugin docs, better-auth.com/pricing; hosted rates from each vendor’s page via our SSO cost guide.

What this page doesn’t price

Security incident response, compliance audits (e.g. SOC 2 evidence for your auth layer), migrations between libraries, and bot/abuse protection are real costs with no published rate, so we leave them out rather than guess. Hosted vendors bundle some of these; check each vendor’s page.
